taxonomyNote: NatureServe: a proposed arrangement would move it to Parasciurus (not accepted per ASM 2024), and it may be conspecific with S. nayaritensis.
fieldMarks: Gray upper body, sometimes yellow patches behind the ears
Tail black above, yellow to brown below, separated by white edging
White underparts, often stained with walnut juice
Total length about 21 in; coat darkens in winter
behavior: Nests in leaf nests in trees or tree cavities
Eats mast, especially walnuts and acorns, pine seeds, flowers, buds and fungi; may eat insects
habitat: Hardwood and mixed oak-pine forest, river valleys and canyons, cottonwood and sycamore groves; ADW gives 1,500-1,900 m elevation in Arizona.
range: Central and southeastern Arizona, west-central New Mexico and northeastern Sonora, Mexico.
